description: Verification contracts per PS2 hardware/runtime component (ids from docs/status/components.json). Hand-written; a contract states what correct means for the component, independently of how it is implemented. Fields with no known answer say 'unknown'. Checked by tools/hwcoverage/hwcoverage.py; coverage of contracts is reported as the contract_specified level.

gs.dither.block: GS pixel pipeline, post-blend colour stage

registers.DIMX (0x44): 16 elements DMyx, 3 bits each at bit 4*(4*y+x), bit 4*(4*y+x)+3 unused; signed range -4..3

functional_requirements: With DTHE=1, DMyx for (x mod 4, y mod 4) of the written pixel is added to R, G and B; alpha is unchanged
The addition happens after alpha blending and before COLCLAMP
Dithering affects frame buffers stored in a 16-bit format (PSMCT16/PSMCT16S) when the 8-bit result is reduced to 5 bits
gs.dither.reset_state: DIMX and DTHE zero after GS reset (PCSX2 GSDrawingEnvironment::Reset); hardware value unknown
gs.dither.read_write_semantics: write-only GS general registers via GIF A+D or PACKED; not readable by the EE
gs.dither.timing: no timing obligation beyond pixel order
acceptance: Unit test: every matrix position, sign handling (-4 vs -1), 4-pixel repetition, order relative to COLCLAMP, no effect with DTHE=0
Hardware: GS frame captures of a dither probe (flat colour quads in PSMCT16 and PSMCT32 over a known DIMX) match bit for bit
references: PCSX2 f0523f8: GSRegs.h GIFRegDIMX, GSState.h ExpandDIMX, GSDrawScanline.cpp WriteFrame
gs.dither.known_divergences: PCSX2 and DobieStation disagree on the element encoding and on whether 32-bit buffers are dithered (decision D-GS-1); unresolved without hardware

gs.alpha.block: GS pixel pipeline, alpha blending and colour clamp

registers.ALPHA_1/2 (0x42/0x43): A, B, C, D selectors and FIX: Cv = ((A - B) * C >> 7) + D
registers.PABE (0x49): bypass blending for source alpha with MSB clear
registers.COLCLAMP (0x46): bit 0: 1 saturates to 0..255, 0 keeps the low 8 bits

functional_requirements: Blend on signed intermediate values without clamping
COLCLAMP selects saturation or wrap after blending and dithering
PABE and FBA as specified per register
gs.alpha.reset_state: COLCLAMP zero after GS reset (PCSX2); the SDK environment sets it to 1
acceptance: Unit tests: saturation and wrap in both directions, PABE, FBA
Hardware: GS frame captures of blend probes
gs.alpha.known_divergences: none between the two references for COLCLAMP

dma.mfifo.block: EE DMAC, memory FIFO between fromSPR (channel 8) and the VIF1 or GIF source chain

registers.D_CTRL (0x1000E000): MFD bits 2-3: 0 none, 2 VIF1, 3 GIF (1 reserved)
registers.D_RBSR (0x1000E040): ring mask; the ring holds RBSR + 16 bytes

functional_requirements: fromSPR writes each qword at RBOR + (MADR & RBSR) and wraps MADR
The drain channel reads tags at RBOR + (TADR & RBSR); data that follows a tag (CNT, NEXT, CALL, RET, END) is read with the same wrap; REF/REFE/REFS data is read in place
The drain stops when it reaches fromSPR's MADR and stays active; MEIS is raised; it continues when fromSPR writes more
Normal completion (END, TIE with IRQ) raises CIS of the drain channel
dma.mfifo.reset_state: D_RBOR, D_RBSR zero after sceDmaReset (existing test); hardware power-on values unknown
dma.mfifo.read_write_semantics: D_RBOR/D_RBSR read back as written; D_STAT status bits clear on write-one, masks toggle on write-one
dma.mfifo.error_behavior: unknown for a ring that crosses invalid memory or a non power-of-two size
dma.mfifo.interrupts: MEIS through INT1 when MEIM is set (DMAC handler cause 14)
dma.mfifo.dma: channel 8 (fromSPR) source; channel 1 (VIF1) or 2 (GIF) drain in source-chain mode
dma.mfifo.timing: unknown: the hardware can stall inside a tag's data; this implementation stalls at tag granularity (D-DMA-2)
acceptance: Unit tests: GIF and VIF1 drains, empty stall with MEIS, resume, END completion, ring wrap of tags and data, REF data in place, fromSPR linear without MFD or outside the ring
Fuzz: DMA harness with MFIFO enabled under ASan
Hardware: MFIFO probe on a physical PS2 (stall point, MEIS timing, MADR/TADR after stall)

dma.stall.block: EE DMAC stall control between a destination (source of data) channel and a source-chain/normal (drain) channel

registers.D_CTRL (0x1000E000): STS bits 4-5: 0 none, 1 SIF0, 2 fromSPR, 3 fromIPU; STD bits 6-7: 0 none, 1 VIF1, 2 GIF, 3 SIF1
registers.D_STADR (0x1000E060): stall address; written by the STS channel with its MADR, writable by the EE

functional_requirements: The STS channel in normal or interleave mode (or at a CNTS destination tag) copies its MADR into D_STADR as it transfers
The STD channel in normal mode, or at a REFS source tag, does not read past D_STADR: it waits while MADR + QWC * 16 > D_STADR
A waiting drain stays active (CHCR.STR set, no CIS) and raises SIS once per stall
The drain continues from where it stopped once D_STADR covers its data (source progress or EE write)
REF, REFE, CNT and the other tags, and channels other than STD, ignore D_STADR
dma.stall.reset_state: D_STADR zero after sceDmaReset (existing test); hardware power-on value unknown
dma.stall.read_write_semantics: D_STADR reads back as written; D_STAT SIS clears on write-one, SIM toggles on write-one
dma.stall.error_behavior: unknown for D_STADR outside the drain's address space or STS/STD naming the same transfer
dma.stall.interrupts: SIS through INT1 when SIM is set (DMAC handler cause 13)
dma.stall.dma: sources SIF0 (5), fromSPR (8), fromIPU (3); drains VIF1 (1), GIF (2), SIF1 (6)
dma.stall.timing: unknown: the references stall per tag (PCSX2) or per block of up to 8 qwords (DobieStation); this implementation checks per REFS tag or whole normal-mode transfer (D-DMA-4)
acceptance: Unit tests: REFS drain waits with SIS and resumes when fromSPR moves D_STADR; normal-mode VIF1 drain resumes on an EE D_STADR write; SIS/SIM/INT1; D_CTRL release; negative controls (REF, STD=0, other drain, exact boundary, STS=0)
